headline: Fed holds rates in a 10-2 split with two hike votes as KOSPI jumps 7.2%
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,744.0 and the 10 year yield sat near 5.04%, while WTI gained 2.2% to 102.06 dollars and Alphabet fell about 10% after hours on its results.

us.text: The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike.
The S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,744.0 and the Nasdaq 0.3% to 26,549.9, with chip stocks doing most of the work.
Alphabet fell about 10% after hours on its first miss in nearly four years, while Microsoft rose on 48% Azure growth.

india.text: Sensex fell 352.64 points to 73,246.03 and the Nifty ended at 22,698.85, dragged by Infosys, Reliance and TCS as crude rose.
FIIs were provisional net buyers of 872 crore rupees in cash on 28 October and DIIs bought 643 crore.
The rupee fell 21 paise to close at 95.28 per dollar on a firmer dollar and surging crude.

global.text: The KOSPI jumped 7.2% to 6,046.5 after SK hynix reported record quarterly profit and a 60 trillion won shareholder payout plan.
Europe ended little changed, with the Stoxx 600 up 0.07% at 644.14 ahead of Thursday's ECB decision.
WTI rose 2.2% to 102.06 dollars on a report that the US told Gulf states to prepare for Iran strikes after the midterms.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold closed the week below 4,000 dollars and now sits 2.4 percent above its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
